text:
jess: Heads up, saw a microburst pattern on pool-3 around 09:12 UTC — short spikes of queue_wait then a kludge of small batches. dumping profiler now.
omar: saw that too. looked like KV cache miss storms right before the spikes? i have a coupling graph.
li: can you paste the profiler snippet? curious if kernel selector switched to fallback kernels during those bursts.
sarah: +1, if kernel falls back we should see a jump in kernel_switch_lat and small_batch_frac.
perf-bot: automated snapshot created: s3://infra-profiles/1961122334/pool3-microburst.tar.gz :eyes:
jess: extracted top lines:
```
profile_summary:
  peak_queue_wait_ms: 180
  p95_queue_wait_ms: 92
  avg_batch_size: 2.1
  small_batch_frac: 0.72
  kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.38
  kernel_selector_fallbacks: 14
```
omar: that small_batch_frac is wild. avg_batch_size 2.1 explains the token-cost spike. we need a histogram over time, not just averages.
li: kernel_selector_fallbacks correlate with kv_cache_miss_rate in the dump. hypothesis: cold KV evictions cause stray long waits which then force scheduler to pack tiny batches to meet latency SLOs.
sarah: what does per-route traffic look like? could be a hot route with short sequences causing fragmentation.
jess: route breakdown in the same window:
```
route A: 42% requests, avg len 18, p95 latency 150ms
route B: 34% requests, avg len 6, p95 latency 210ms
route C (re-ranker): 18% requests, avg len 2, p95 latency 300ms
```
omar: route C is the killer — super short sequences and high p95. scheduler ends up dispatching immediately instead of waiting to batch.
li: proposal: add two things to observability
  1) token-level stacked latency waterfall by route (kernel time vs queue wait vs kv wait)
  2) batch_size histogram heatmap (time x batch_size) with percentiles and a small_batch_ratio metric
we should also emit kernel_selector_reason tag (e.g., "kv_miss","max_seq","fallback_kernel") so dashboards can pivot.
sarah: agree. also add a KV cache occupancy metric per node + approximate TTL churn. eviction storms would show up there.
jess: quick prometheus query ideas:
- rate(runtime_queue_wait_ms_bucket[5m]) to build queue wait histograms
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(runtime_batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- increase(runtime_kv_miss_total[5m]) / increase(runtime_kv_lookup_total[5m]) as kv_miss_rate
li: for kernel selector tags: instrument the selector to emit runtime_kernel_choice{reason="kv_miss"} increment when it selects fallback.
omar: visualization: stacked area for p50/p95 queue_wait + stacked bars for avg_batch_size; overlay kernel_fallback_count as red points.
sarah: ops question: do we want the scheduler to wait 5-10ms more for tiny routes to avoid tiny batches? risk is p95 for short routes goes up.
jess: we can test a conservative delay for route C only (10ms) behind a feature flag, compare cost/perf delta. run canary on pool-3.
perf-bot: created ticket INF-4921: "microburst: route-C small-batch mitigation + dashboards" and assigned to @jess @li @omar
omar: i'll prototype the batch_size heatmap and a KV eviction chart. will push a prometheus exporter patch to add kernel_selector_reason.
li: i'll add an annotation to the continuous-batching dashboard and a new panel for per-route waterfall. keeping it lightweight.
sarah: let's also add an alert: if small_batch_frac > 0.6 and kv_miss_rate > 0.2 for 2m, fire perf-oncall.
jess: sounds good. i'll run the 10ms delay canary tonight and post results here. thanks all :thumbsup:
perf-bot: ticket INF-4921 updated: milestone = next-sprint, priority = P2
